lessons.title: Health awareness: HIV/AIDS and drug abuse

objectives: Explain what HIV and AIDS are
Describe how HIV is and is not transmitted
Describe prevention, testing, treatment and stigma
Explain the dangers of drugs and alcohol misuse and how to resist pressure
reviewNotes: Health content to be reviewed by a qualified health worker before release (transmission facts, prevention wording, treatment statements); no medical advice or dosages are given; local services should be added by teachers.

Draft for teacher review: content is general and non-political; legal ages, institutions, names of laws and any health or road-safety statement must be verified (by a teacher, and for health topics by a health worker) before release.

blocks.md: **HIV** (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) is a virus that attacks the body's defence system. Without treatment it can lead to **AIDS** (Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome), when the body can no longer fight many infections. **Treatment** with antiretroviral medicines (**ART**), taken regularly under medical supervision, helps people with HIV to live long and healthy lives and greatly reduces the chance of passing on the virus.

blocks.caption: Facts about HIV
blocks.alt: Two columns showing how HIV is transmitted and how it is not.

blocks.title: Transmission
blocks.md: HIV is passed on through: **unprotected sex** with an infected person; **infected blood** (transfusion of unscreened blood, sharing needles, razors or other sharp instruments); and **from mother to child** during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding. It is **not** passed on by hugging, shaking hands, sharing food or cups, toilets, coughing, mosquito bites or ordinary living together.

blocks.title: Prevention and support
blocks.md: Prevention: **abstinence** for young people, being faithful to one tested partner, correct and consistent use of **condoms** for those who are sexually active, never sharing sharp objects, using only screened blood, and **testing and treatment** (including for pregnant women). Know your status by testing at a health facility. **Stigma and discrimination** against people with HIV are wrong: they discourage testing and treatment. People with HIV deserve respect, care and the same rights as others.

**Drugs and alcohol.** Drug abuse means taking substances such as alcohol, tobacco, cannabis, or misusing medicines for non-medical reasons. Dangers: damage to the **brain and body**, addiction, poor school results, accidents, violence, risky behaviour, crime, family and money problems. Reasons why young people start include **peer pressure**, curiosity, stress or family problems. **Resisting**: say no firmly, avoid risky situations, choose friends who support you, talk to a trusted adult, and seek help early.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Medical advice must come from qualified health workers: this lesson gives general awareness only.
- Do not judge or avoid a person with HIV; support them.
- Never use any medicine that was not prescribed or that is not meant for you.

blocks.title: Example 1: true or false?
blocks.statement: Is HIV transmitted by sharing a meal with an infected person?
steps: HIV is not spread through food or utensils.
It needs blood, sexual fluids or breast milk to be transmitted.
blocks.answer: No, it is not transmitted by sharing a meal.

blocks.title: Example 2: peer pressure
blocks.statement: A friend offers you a cigarette at a party. Give two ways to respond.
steps: Say no firmly and give your reason.
Leave the situation or suggest another activity.
Talk to a trusted adult if you feel pressured.
blocks.answer: Say no and leave; tell a trusted adult.
